topics.name: Similes with as ... as and like
Future with will and first conditional

options: The evening was as softer as silk.
The evening was as soft as silk.
The evening was as soft than silk.
questions.rule: A simile with as ... as uses the plain adjective between the two as: as soft as.

options: I have finished my homework already.
I have finish my homework already.
I has finished my homework already.
questions.rule: Present perfect = have/has + past participle. With I, use have finished.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: The pattern is as + adjective + as: as tall as. Never mix as with than.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: With a singular subject like Priya, the present perfect uses has: has written.
Complete the simile with the second as: as cold as ice.
The bird is singular, so the present perfect is has flown.

questions.prompt: Make a sentence with a simile.
questions.rule: A simile compares two things using like or as: the baby's smile is like sunshine.

chat: Will you come to the beach with us tomorrow?
options: Yes, I will come with you.
Yes, I will came with you.
questions.rule: After will, use the base form of the verb: will come.

questions.source: No other girl in the class is as tall as Asha.
options: Asha is tallest than any other girl in the class.
Asha is taller than any other girl in the class.
Asha is taller than any girl in the class.
questions.rule: Positive no other ... as tall as becomes comparative taller than any other. Asha is a girl too, so keep other.
In the present perfect, put not after has: has not stopped.

questions.prompt: Which sentence talks about the future correctly?
options: The bird will flew away soon.
The bird will flying away soon.
The bird will fly away soon.
questions.rule: Simple future = will + base verb: will fly.

options: Spring is the most brightest season of the year.
Spring is the brightest season of the year.
Spring is the brighter season of the year.
questions.rule: Comparing one with many needs the superlative: the brightest. Never use most with -est.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: Use for with a length of time (for five years) and since with a starting point (since 2020).

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: Have needs the past participle: have you ever seen, not saw.

questions.after: carry your bag to the bus stop.
questions.rule: To offer help or promise something, use will + base verb: I will carry.
than compares two things, so use the comparative: costlier than.
Present perfect question: Has + subject + past participle: Has the young bird learnt ...?
Answer in the same tense: I have finished (have + past participle).

chat: How was the sea at Alibag?
options: It was as calm as a lake.
It were as calm as a lake.
It was as calmer as a lake.
questions.rule: It takes was, and the simile keeps the plain adjective: as calm as.

questions.source: The children will sing a song.
options: Will the children sang a song?
Will the children sing a song?
Do the children will sing a song?
questions.rule: Move will to the front and keep the base verb: Will the children sing ...?

questions.prompt: Pick the sentence with the correct tense.
options: We have gone to the beach last Sunday.
We went to the beach last Sunday.
We go to the beach last Sunday.
questions.rule: A finished time like last Sunday needs the simple past (went), not the present perfect.

options: The clouds look like white sheep.
The clouds looks like white sheep.
The clouds look likes white sheep.
questions.rule: Plural clouds takes look, and like in a simile never changes: look like.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: taller is already comparative, so don't add more. Use much taller to make it stronger.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: Between as ... as use the plain adjective: as blue as the sky.

questions.after: in Mumbai since he was five.
questions.rule: since + a starting point goes with the present perfect: has lived.

questions.before: If you water the seeds every day, they
questions.after: into small plants by next month.
questions.rule: First conditional: If + simple present, will + base verb: they will grow.

questions.prompt: Make a sentence about the future.
questions.rule: Subject + will + base verb + place: The children will play in the rain.

chat: Which season do you like best?
options: I like spring the best because it is the most colourful season.
I like spring the better because it is the more colourful season.
I like spring the best because it is the colourfullest season.
questions.rule: Long adjectives form the superlative with the most: the most colourful.

chat: When did you get your new bicycle?
options: I have got it last week.
questions.rule: last week is a finished time, so use the simple past: I got it.

questions.prompt: Rewrite using 'not as ... as', beginning with 'Sameer'.
options: Sameer is as tall as Ravi.
Sameer is not as tall as Ravi.
Sameer is not as taller as Ravi.
questions.rule: A is taller than B = B is not as tall as A. Use the plain adjective with as ... as.

options: If you help me, I will help you too.
If you will help me, I help you too.
If you helps me, I will help you too.
questions.rule: First conditional: If + simple present (you help), then will + base verb.

options: Dadi have lived in this house since 1990.
Dadi has lived in this house for 1990.
Dadi has lived in this house since 1990.
questions.rule: Dadi is singular: has lived. A year is a starting point, so use since 1990.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: After will always use the base form: will become.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: who refers to Neha (one person), so the verb is lives.
its shows belonging (the bird's wings). it's means it is.
If + simple present, then will + base verb: If it rains, we will stay indoors.
Comparative + than compares two things: warmer than yesterday.

chat: Can we go to the park this evening?
options: If it will stop raining, we go.
If it stop raining, we will go.
If it stops raining, we will go.
questions.rule: In the if part use the simple present (it stops); in the result part use will.

questions.source: If you do not hurry, you will miss the bus.
options: Unless you hurry, you will miss the bus.
Unless you do not hurry, you will miss the bus.
Unless you hurry, you missed the bus.
questions.rule: Unless already means if not, so drop do not: Unless you hurry.
Move has to the front and keep the past participle: Has Kiran seen ...?

options: The Pacific is larger than any ocean in the world.
The Pacific is largest than any other ocean.
The Pacific is larger than any other ocean.
questions.rule: The Pacific is itself an ocean, so compare it with any other ocean: larger than any other.

questions.prompt: Pick the sentence with the correct tense.
options: Yesterday the sea shines like a mirror under a cloudless sky.
Yesterday the sea has shone like a mirror under a cloudless sky.
Yesterday the sea shone like a mirror under a cloudless sky.
questions.rule: Yesterday is a finished time, so use the simple past: shone.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: of all compares more than two, so use the superlative: the most beautiful.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: After will, use the base verb: will miss.
one of the + superlative + plural noun: one of the finest poems.

questions.prompt: Make a sentence in the present perfect.
questions.rule: has lived ... since 2015: the present perfect shows an action that started in the past and still goes on.

chat: How long have you known Meena?
options: I have knew her since Class 2.
I have known her since Class 2.
questions.rule: From a past point till now, use the present perfect: have known (past participle of know).

chat: Which bus should I take, the red one or the blue one?
options: Take the blue one. It is more faster, so you will reach on time.
Take the blue one. It is faster, so you will reach on time.
Take the blue one. It is faster, so you will reached on time.
questions.rule: Comparing two buses: faster (no more). After will use the base verb reach.

questions.source: Spring is the most pleasant season of the year.
options: No other season of the year is more pleasant as spring.
No other season of the year is as pleasant as spring.
No other season of the year is as pleasant than spring.
questions.rule: Superlative the most pleasant becomes positive No other ... is as pleasant as.

options: The future will be exciting, will it?
The future will be exciting, won't it?
The future will be exciting, isn't it?
questions.rule: A positive sentence with will takes a negative tag with won't: won't it?
